chapter: The band's later history and Cootie Williams
title: The Excelsior band's following and its younger players
summary: The band drew crowds at Mardi Gras; it now plays only once a year under Edward Langston, with young players.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Give all the information. Make it honest now while you're in. I'm calling. I don't. Good. Looked like you brought your band. So I says, the seltzer band. So I put it in the announcement. I says, the seltzer band's going to play. So then I asked one of the men, I says, now what's this seltzer band? They said, the men always say, well, that's the excelsior band. The seltzer band. So that's another phase of your evening.

Well, I tell you, we were the drawing card back in those days, you know. Every time we mentioned the seltzer band, I meant the public was coming out. That's pretty well. I'm saying the seltzer band now is, would be seven, six years old.
Did the band have a large following, a second line, as they say?

Yes, yes, yes. And sometimes they had to have an officer, you understand, to take the crowd away. Really? But if you have Mardi Gras, you would have probably five or six bands, you know, and the seltzer band had the crowd. And the masters, you know, on the foot, they would be hung for the seltzer band. I can hear them now calling for folk. You know what I mean? The seltzer band with them. Yes.
And now they only play on a conical day, do they? Just once a year. Once a year. And who is the leader now?

Langston. Edward Langston. Edward Langston. Yeah, I wish I could have gotten known to him by that time I'd have him here with me. He's a trumpet player, is he? No, he's a saxophone player. Saxophone. And saxophone. We'll see in our next trip, then we'll find him. Yes. I'll try to get him something, you know, kind of intelligently. As I'm saying right now, I don't know just what I'm talking about. This is very good.
You see, there's a good history of it. But I imagine they play a different style to the way the old band used to play.

Well, I don't think so. You don't think they have? Because we played all the popular... Of course, you know, as a whole, music has changed a little bit, you know. Yes. I think back to my days, music was more simplified than what it is right now.
Yes. What sort of age would you say the men in the band are today? The average age of the men in the band today?

What is playing today? Yes. Oh, they're around... In the 20s, I should think. Oh, they're young. They're young. 30 years old. Are there any old time now? Well, all those time has practically died out in the last few years. That did play along with those youngsters. Yes.
Next year, about the oldest one now. That's 11.
Oh, next door would be somewhere else... We have the 60s. Any 60s? No, I won't say he's that old. Around 60 years old. Yes. 58, 60 years old.
